title: WISE photocentres of Project Hephaistos Dyson-sphere candidates A and E lag their Gaia motion in 2014-2024, so part of their infrared light comes from a stationary background source
abstract: Question: Project Hephaistos found M dwarfs with a mid-infrared excess that a partial Dyson sphere can fit; later work proposed background dust-obscured AGN. Circumstellar material moves with the star, but a background source does not. If a fraction f of the WISE W1/W2 (3.4/4.6 um) light is stationary, the WISE photocentre moves at (1 - f) times the Gaia DR3 proper motion. Method: we fitted the motion of NEOWISE-R single-exposure positions (2014-2024) relative to Gaia DR3 for all ten candidates of Ren et al. (2026), with per-visit field correction from 60 local stars. The null is 1,447 isolated moving field stars near the candidates, processed with the same pipeline. Results: candidate A lags with f = 0.072 +- 0.022 (z = -3.1; 2 of 325 W1-matched null stars lag as much), in agreement with an earlier independent campaign fit (0.058 +- 0.020). Candidate E lags with f = 0.16 +- 0.07 (z = -2.2, p = 0.03). As a group, the nine candidates without the known AGN case G lag more than the null (p = 0.021). The other candidates have errors of 0.07-0.21 in f and give no individual result. The null stars and 179 high-proper-motion red dwarfs give median f near 0. With the W1-W2 colour excess, the stationary sources of A and E have W1 about 15.0 and 15.5 and AGN-like W1-W2 about 0.7. If they also make the 22 um excess, W2-W4 is 7.5 and 6.4, as for dust-obscured AGN. No candidate varies in W1/W2 more than field controls. We also show that the IRSA AllWISE multi-epoch table repeats the fixed AllWISE catalogue position (epoch 2010.56) in each row, so its rows are not 2010 astrometric epochs. Conclusion: for A and E, part of the infrared light is not circumstellar, which supports background contamination over a Dyson-sphere explanation. Limitations: the test measures only 3-5 um light; the 12-22 um excess is not tested directly; A survives a ten-candidate correction only marginally (empirical Bonferroni p 0.09); D and I stay unconstrained.

display.caption: WISE W1/W2 photocentre minus the Gaia DR3 position of the star, along the proper-motion direction, after per-visit field correction (NEOWISE visit medians, 2014-2024). A line with zero slope means that all light moves with the star. The orange line is the fit; slope = -f |pm|. A and E lag. F and J do not. The open square is the AllWISE catalogue position at 2010.56, which is not used in the fit.

Left: photocentre velocity residual along the proper motion against W1 for 1,447 isolated moving field stars near the candidates (grey, same pipeline) and for the ten candidates (blue; G, the known background AGN case, orange). Right: z of each candidate against the W1-matched null distribution. Mean z of the nine candidates without G = -0.80, p = 0.021.

Stationary fraction f of the W1/W2 photocentre for each candidate. Filled circles: NEOWISE 2014-2024 (primary). Open squares: with the AllWISE 2010.56 position added. Grey bands: 68 and 95 percent of matched moving field stars, converted to f for each candidate. Green diamond: f predicted for D by its catalogued Legacy DR10 galaxy at 3.0 arcsec.

citations.reason: Introduced the WISE-Gaia co-motion (photocentre lag) test that we use; its fit of candidate A (kappa 0.942 +- 0.020) agrees with ours. We note that its AllWISE MEP rows are fixed catalogue positions; its NEOWISE-only variant agrees.
Related NEOWISE study of 12 um-excess field dwarfs and their variability; uses similar NEOWISE visit methods.
Project Hephaistos II: the Dyson-sphere candidates. Our motion test shows stationary infrared light in candidates A and E.
Proposed background hot DOG contamination of the candidates.
Source of the ten candidate identifiers and of the archival centroid, imaging and radio diagnostics; our time-domain result supports contamination for A and E.
